title: Drinking at dances and cabarets during Prohibition
summary: No bars at private dances; bring your own bottle; cabarets like Tranchina's and the Halfway House; the Little Club as the priciest.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Cabarets, honky-tonks and the Storyville nightlife scene

blocks.x: How did prices run in the bars?

Well, there were no bars in the dancers that I'm talking about. Remember, these were dancers that were given by, in most cases, private clubs and no bars. The bottle was out in the automobile and he went out during intermission and got a couple of slugs and... But, uh... They were never given... When I say they were given... For instance, I mentioned the old Sazerac bar. I didn't mean that that was a ballroom at the time that we gave these dancers. It had ceased to be a bar for quite some years and was rented out to individuals for parties and dances and whatnot. But we had no bar set up in these places at all. They either had a flask on your hip or a bottle in the automobile if you happened to have a car or something of that side. Now, in the cases, of course, in the case of Tranchinas and the Halfway House, well, those were nightclubs or cabarets or what have you. And, of course, you could buy a drink. But even in those places, in many cases, you brought your own bottle.
That was Prohibition Town. That's right. What were they selling?
Well, would it be beer or wine or spirits or something? Well, yes.

Of course, this was many years ago. But I won't mention any names. But in many places, it wasn't supposed to sell whiskey. You could buy whiskey. It may be served in a demitasse coffee cup. But it was to be had in a great many places.
I guess, how would prices run, though, in those places? Like the Little Club or the Halfway House?

Well, now, I don't remember exactly. But in the case of the Little Club, I would say that it was probably the most expensive club in the city at that time. And demanded and got better prices than anywhere else. It was—they always came up with good talent and good bands and good entertainment, so they got the price.
Would it run a dollar and a half for a glass of gin or something? Or would it be fifty cents?
I don't recall. And I don't recall if you could buy whiskey in the club or not. It may have been that you had to bring your own. I don't recall that.
